tob-10096: Richard Rolle, a fourteenth-century English hermit, writes plain guides to the contemplative life for ordinary readers. tob-10496: Julian of Norwich, an English anchoress who lived walled into a small cell by a church, recorded sixteen visions of Christ’s love in what became the first book in English known to be written by a woman. tob-0096: Johann Weyer — leech to the Duke of Cleves — penned the first doctor’s broadside at the witch-hunts, holding accused witches for gloomy old women, not devil-worshippers. tob-4096: H. Kern’s Englishing of the Lotus Sutra — the Saddharma Pundarika — gives one of Buddhism’s best-loved scriptures. Its parables of the burning house and the lost son preach rescue for all. Kern’s scholar’s version graced the Sacred Books of the East.
tob-10796: Arthur Lloyd’s Hinduism and Buddhism — An Historical Sketch — traces the two faiths from the Vedas through their spread across Asia. The missionary-scholar wrote with sympathy and learning. The book remains a clear historical introduction to the Eastern religions.
a-brief-history-of-the-united-states-pg6: John Bach McMaster, one of the great tellers of the nation's past, sums up the story of the United States for students in this clear, trusted textbook. arxiv-2605-08896: A model can be right and still fragile — one nudge to the input flips its answer. arxiv-2605-08996: Symbolic accelerators crunch graph-structured computations, but bloated graphs waste silicon. arxiv-2605-09096: Neural operators learn mappings between whole functions — fields, not just vectors — and U-Nets organize computation hierarchically. arxiv-2605-09196: Rigid bodies — tumbling boxes, clanking robots — obey strict dynamics that transformers were not built for. arxiv-2605-09296: AI-generated images look perfect at a glance but betray themselves in microscopic statistical defects invisible to the eye. The 2026 paper catches synthetic images by their tiny tells.
arxiv-2605-09496: Reasoning in LLMs may live in subspaces that do not care about format — math, code, prose all share the machinery. Aojie Yuan and Zhiyuan Su look beyond language for format-agnostic reasoning subspaces. The 2026 paper hunts the universal circuitry of thought.
arxiv-2605-09596: Muonic atoms — with a heavy muon orbiting instead of an electron — probe the nucleus exquisitely, and the nucleus is not a point. Doğa Yaşar and Bastian Sikora compute finite nuclear size corrections to hyperfine structure. The 2026 paper is precision atomic physics.
arxiv-2605-09696: Discovering a system's governing equations from data needs the right basis functions — and choosing them by hand is deeply limiting. arxiv-2605-09796: Misophonia — when everyday sounds trigger rage or panic — is poorly understood, and sufferers' voices go unheard. arxiv-2606-16996: ActiveSAM makes open-vocabulary image segmentation faster by pruning the label list on the fly. arxiv-2606-17096: Jiguang Yu and colleagues analyze how sound-absorbing walls affect the stability of fast airflows. arxiv-2606-17696: Jizong Zhan releases FllumaOne, a code-native multimodal CAD dataset with executable programs and kernel-validated geometry. Each design is real code that runs, not just pictures. arxiv-2606-17796: A. Anju and P. G. Romeo study cross-connections of the normed algebra of finite rank bounded operators on a Hilbert space. The algebraic structure links operator theory to category-like frameworks. The paper extends functional analysis into new organizational territory.
plos-pone-0003396: Brain scanners revealed pain rewriting the brain in this 2008 study. plos-pone-0003496: Tuberculosis researchers spotlighted a master switch in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003596: Kidney researchers found an alarm receptor driving reperfusion damage in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003696: In 2008, Pinto, Melo-Cristino, and Ramirez built a better yardstick for microbe sorting. plos-pone-0003796: Premi, Srivastava, and Panneer found a patchwork Y chromosome in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003896: A 2008 stem-cell study got lab-grown heart cells multiplying. Yamanaka, Zahanich, and Wersto boosted proliferation in monolayer cultures of ES-derived cardiomyocytes. The enhanced growth brings replacement heart tissue a step closer to reality.
plos-pone-0003996: In 2008, Sabath, Landan, and Graur solved a puzzle of genes written over each other. Their method estimated selection strength separately for each overlapping gene in the pair. plos-pone-0004096: In 2009, Moorthy, Gupta, and Bhosale probed a life-saving trade-off in India. Single and extended nevirapine doses cut breast-milk HIV transmission in Indian infants. plos-pone-0004196: In 2009, Mostowy, Tham, and Danckaert found cell scaffolds fighting germs. Septins regulated bacterial entry into host cells. The filament proteins helped cells resist invasion. plos-pone-0004396: In 2009, two researchers questioned mitochondrial DNA's odd cross-animal sameness. Proof of change in animal mitochondrial DNA breeding-group size was found. The textbook constancy cracked at last. The neat finding reshapes gene history. The work reopens a quiet old debate.
plos-pone-0004496: In 2009, Koslowski, Kübler, and Chamaillard linked a gene switch to chronic gut disease. Wnt factor TCF-4 variants tracked ileal Crohn's disease closely. The defensin regulator's variants raised risk. The finding maps gut immunity genetics. The Paneth cells were the key.
plos-pone-0004596: In 2009, Marguet, Lubrano, and Gueudin found the virus deciding the baby's illness. In very young infants, bronchiolitis severity depended on carried viruses. plos-pone-0004696: In 2009, Debily, El Marhomy, and Boulanger mapped a breast-cancer protein's network. A working network tied to PIP in breast cancer was built. The gene's contradictory roles were explored. The study informs oncology research today. The odd protein is milk-linked.
plos-pone-0358596: University teachers are adopting generative AI — or quietly resisting it. The results tell universities what actually drives lasting AI adoption in teaching, beyond the initial hype.
plos-pone-0354696: Yellow fever mosquitoes shrug off many repellents — but hemp might faze them. plos-pone-0357796: Mastitis costs dairy farmers dearly — and Sahiwal cattle deserve better defenses. plos-pone-0357296: Mesenchymal stromal cells can donate their mitochondria to failing neighbor cells — cellular organ transplants. plos-pone-0354796: Men and women read social cues differently — and the gap widens where social function is impaired. plos-pone-0354096: Asiatic lions — fewer than a thousand remain — desperately need room beyond their single stronghold. plos-pone-0335296: Leopards share Sri Lankan farmland with people — by keeping carefully different hours. plos-pone-0357496: Careers should sustain people, not consume them. plos-pone-0356796: Carbon monoxide poisoning disrupts the body’s breathing chemistry in surprisingly complex ways. plos-pone-0356496: Who receives invasive coronary angiography isn’t determined by medical need alone. plos-pone-0355996: Detecting milk fat content demands highly sensitive sensors. This paper used hybrid machine learning to optimize a multilayer surface plasmon resonance sensor for high-sensitivity milk fat detection. The optimized sensor guards dairy quality with precision the industry can trust.
plos-pone-0355196: Mosquitoes are evolving cross-resistance that defeats multiple insecticides at once. plos-pone-0357096: The desert rose plant may hide weapons against lung cancer. plos-pone-0356996: The pupil betrays where attention goes — if you know how to read it. The method reads focus straight from the eyes, opening new possibilities for attention research.
plos-pone-0356596: Anti-VEGF eye injections save sight in wet macular degeneration — but bleeding inside the eye is a feared complication. plos-pone-0356696: Growing up alongside an autistic sibling shapes a childhood in profound, rarely studied ways. plos-pone-0355396: Early recovery from alcohol use disorder is when relapse risk runs highest — and predicting lapses could save lives. plos-pone-0351296: Qurayyah Painted Ware — striking ancient pottery from Arabia — tells a story of branding millennia before marketing. This paper traced its genesis, transformation, and diffusion. plos-pone-0356296: People with HIV who smoke face compounded heart risks — and nicotine metabolism speed may modulate them. The findings could personalize smoking cessation and cardiac prevention in this vulnerable group.
plos-pone-0354896: Osteosarcoma — bone cancer — demands fast, accurate MRI diagnosis. plos-pone-0355296: Can digital health tools ease loneliness in older adults — or do they deepen isolation? The planned review will separate the technologies that genuinely connect from those that merely distract.
plos-pone-0355596: Immersive VR training generates rich physiological data — if sensors and AI can interpret it. The synthesis charts a field poised to make virtual training genuinely adaptive to learners’ bodies.
plos-pone-0350296: Heart disease driven by salty diets and kidney dysfunction will burden G20 nations for decades. The sixty-year projections are a policy alarm bell — showing where prevention could avert millions of cardiac deaths.
plos-pone-0355496: DNA barcoding generates oceans of data on the BOLD platform — and researchers need better tools. BOLDconnectR is an R package for streamlined retrieval, transformation, and analysis of BOLD barcode data. The open-source package democratizes large-scale biodiversity informatics.
plos-pone-0346396: Chinese social media burns with workplace burnout discourse — and computation can map it. This paper analyzed the discourse, sentiment, and resonance of burnout on Chinese social media. The findings reveal how an entire generation articulates exhaustion — and what that collective voice demands.
plos-pone-0353796: Bone marrow stromal cells — imaged by fluorescence microscopy — need automated segmentation for research at scale. plos-pone-0346996: Begonia fimbristipula — a Chinese medicinal plant — faces a newly reported leaf spot enemy. This paper is the first report of Corynespora cassiicola causing the disease in China. The finding alerts growers and botanists to a pathogen threatening a valued species.
plos-pone-0343196: Distribution networks — with virtual power plants assisting — need optimized load transfer. This paper developed expert-guided optimization for that task. The findings help grid operators keep power flowing reliably as renewables and distributed resources reshape the electrical landscape.
plos-pone-0337296: Elite freestyle aerial skiers — their balance control — can be classified by AI fusing multiple data streams. This paper built dual-stream deep learning for multimodal feature fusion in that classification. The findings reveal the balance signatures of world-class aerialists — with applications to training and injury prevention.
plos-pone-0354596: Problematic consumption — shopping, gaming, eating — involves cognitive flexibility, impulsivity, and compulsivity in tangled ways. This paper examined all three. The analysis disentangled which cognitive traits drive which compulsive behaviors. The findings move beyond ‘addiction’ as a single label — toward targeted interventions for distinct psychological profiles.
plos-pone-0353696: Wilms tumor — CDCA8 regulating ATP5F1A protein stability and malignant behavior. This paper uncovered the mechanism with prognostic implications. The molecular chain linked a cell division protein to energy metabolism in childhood kidney cancer. The findings nominate targets for a disease where treatment is already brutal.
plos-pone-0353996: Chinese urbanites’ expressed happiness — uneven — unraveled from geotagged social media. This paper identified key predictors and future climate-happiness links. plos-pone-0343896: Underwater caves — vertebrate site formation’s neotaphonomic characteristics. This paper documented them. The findings revealed how bones accumulate and preserve in submerged caverns. The research served both paleontology and forensics — the underwater archive, read correctly.
plos-pone-0353196: Eastern North Pacific killer whales — essential and non-essential elements in their tissues. This paper measured concentrations. The findings revealed the chemical burden apex predators carry. The research monitored ocean health — through the bodies of its orcas.
plos-pone-0349096: Spring water pathogens — their bacterial diversity, quantitative risk, and biocontrol through phyto-biosorbents. This paper assessed all three. The risk analysis quantified what lurks in natural springs. The findings offered plant-based purification — biosorbents as the low-cost guardian of drinking water.
plos-pone-0341096: Lung nodule segmentation and malignancy classification — two-stage — via adaptive geometric-attention networks in federated edge healthcare IoT. This paper built it. The privacy-preserving design learned across hospitals without sharing data. The findings advanced the distributed AI — cancer detection that respects patient privacy.
plos-pone-0353396: Tanzanian children aged six to fifty-nine months — Shiga toxin E. coli O157:H7 prevalence, virulence, and antibiotic susceptibility in Longido. This paper mapped all three. plos-pone-0352696: Inflammatory bowel disease — perceived stigma, more than a digestive disorder. This paper studied it. The analysis captured the shame beyond the symptoms. plos-pone-0352096: Evidence seeking, reasoning, and cognitive reflection — patterns via supervised clustering. This paper studied them. The analysis grouped the thinkers by their habits. plos-pone-0348096: Post-COVID express delivery services — will public attention show new trends? This paper asked. The analysis tracked the parcel boom’s attention arc. plos-pone-0351396: Lebanese pregnant women — the 12-point Mediterranean Diet Adherence Screener’s validity and internal consistency. This paper explored them. europmc-pmc2861696: White blood cells cast DNA nets to snare fungi, and this 2010 paper studies the trick against Aspergillus. europmc-pmc2909996: Identifying fungi from soil DNA needs a reliable barcode. This 2010 paper tests ITS as an environmental DNA barcode for fungi with computer simulations, revealing potential PCR biases. The authors' in silico probe warns of skewed results. Their caution improved fungal surveys.
europmc-pmc2913796: Obesity smolders with low-grade inflammation that never quite goes out. europmc-pmc3034196: RTX proteins form a huge toxin clan. This 2010 review covers the sprawling RTX family, all shipped out by one secretion system. The authors survey the clan's tricks. europmc-pmc3098796: Stem cell trials got a field guide. This 2011 paper surveys clinical trials testing stem cell therapies. The authors map the crowded landscape. Their overview guides the field. Eye and heart trials led the pack. The guide warns of unproven clinics.
europmc-pmc3115896: Metabolic syndrome's definition got debated. This 2011 paper reviews definitions and controversies around metabolic syndrome. The authors sort the competing criteria. europmc-pmc3125296: The rubber hand trick got dissected. This 2011 paper finds body ownership and proprioceptive drift diverge in the rubber hand illusion. The authors split the two measures. europmc-pmc3366996: Mouth germs revealed gum disease. This 2012 paper deep-sequences mouth microbes for gum-disease signatures. The authors reveal the markers. Their work guides dentistry. Liu's team led the work. The paper is widely cited. It shaped dental diagnostics. The study is a classic.
europmc-pmc3368796: Scar tissue got a master switch. This 2012 paper shows the CTGF protein drives fibrosis and blocking it reverses scarring. The authors reveal the reversal. Their work points to drugs. Lipson's team led the work. The paper is widely cited. The study shaped fibrosis research.

europmc-pmc3403996: Engineered immune cells got a brain delivery. This 2012 paper shows engineered Tregs suppress MS-like disease via nose drops. The authors reveal the suppression. Their work points to MS therapy. Fransson's team led the work. The paper is widely cited.
europmc-pmc6510296: Mitochondria are the cell's power plants, and when they falter, the body may stop responding properly to insulin - a hallmark of type 2 diabetes. europmc-pmc6517696: Bacteriophages are viruses that kill bacteria while leaving human cells alone - a tempting weapon against drug-resistant infections. europmc-pmc6519796: Standard heart-disease risk scores use a handful of factors and miss many future patients. europmc-pmc6621996: Systematic reviews take months of expert slog - much of it automatable. europmc-pmc6702196: A blood draw might forecast how long you live. Scanning the metabolic profiles of 44,168 people, researchers found chemical signatures tied to the risk of dying from any cause. europmc-pmc6770596: Salt and blood pressure are old adversaries - and the evidence still favors less salt. This review confirms the sodium-hypertension link: cutting salt lowers pressure and trims hypertension risk. The familiar advice stands on solid ground.
europmc-pmc6770896: Triple-negative breast cancer is the toughest subtype - no hormone targets, relentless growth. Chemotherapy is the main weapon, but resistance comes fast. europmc-pmc6804896: Head and neck cancers that return after care face grim odds - immune therapy changed that. europmc-pmc6903396: E-cigarettes changed teen tobacco use - the numbers tell how. This CDC report tracked tobacco product use among US middle and high school students in 2019. The shifts guide action. Vapes boomed while smokes fell. The data arm schools and parents.
europmc-pmc6912996: Forecast models can be boldly wrong - tuning fixes that. This paper says tuning is the weak heel of forecasting number-crunching: risk models must match truth. The skipped measure gets its due. A model that mistunes lies. AI needs this truth check.
